_note: Loading-screen lines. kind 'tip' is always eligible; kind 'lore' needs the region in 'after' to have been reached (null: from the start). Keep every line free of anything the player has not yet seen.

tips.text: A parry answers a blow from the side it comes from. Watch the shoulder, not the blade.
A parry made at the last instant costs nothing and leaves the guardian open for longer.
The shield stops what you cannot read, and charges you stamina for it. Raise it at the last instant and it charges nothing.
Dodging early is safe. Dodging late is safe and earns you an opening.
An empty stamina bar is the most dangerous thing you carry. Let it fill before you commit.
Every guardian repeats itself. The first death is the price of learning the rhythm; the knowledge is yours afterwards.
When a seam of light opens on a staggered foe, cut along it. Cutting across it does nothing.
Sequences are found by trying them. The yard behind the sanctuary has a foe that will stand still for it.
A full surge breaks a foe in the middle of its attack. Spend it on the blow you cannot answer any other way.
The relic at your belt mends a third of you, and then needs time. It will not let you waste it at full health.
Two-handed weapons leave no hand for a shield. Decide which you trust more before you set out.
Heavy weapons answer to strength, quick ones to dexterity. Putting points where your weapon does not look wastes them.
Fight with a piece of equipment long enough and you master it. Each mastery is a point to spend.
Dying costs you the road, not what you carried. Gold, experience and anything found stay with you.
A lever pulled stays pulled. The short road it opens is there on every later journey.
A shrine restores more than half of you. It is usually worth the detour before a guardian.
Chests off the road are opened once. What is in them does not come back; a few coins sometimes do.
Some stretches of road offer a second fight nobody asked you to take. They pay better than the road does.
Orren can make a blade better than it was. He cannot make it a different blade.
If the windows for parrying feel unkind, Forgiving Timing in the settings widens them. Nothing is withheld for using it.
A staggered foe takes more from every cut. That is the time for your longest sequence, not your safest.
Frost slows the arm and flame keeps biting after the blow. Resistance blunts both.
You can turn back from any stop on the road. The sanctuary does not judge it.
The records you find are not decoration. Enough of them, and a third choice opens at the end.
Nobody alive remembers the kingdom being lit. The lamps along the old roads are taken for shrines, and people leave bread at them.
The sanctuary bell has no rope. It rings anyway, each time you come back.
Vaelora's maps still mark the royal roads. Nothing has been carried along them in three hundred years.
Lyra speaks from the walls of the sanctuary. She says she has been waiting, and will not yet say for how long.
Orren kept the forge lit because somebody told him to, once. He has stopped wondering who.
The garrison of the Fallen Courtyard was never relieved. Most of it is still at its posts.
The statues in the courtyard have had their faces cut away. The hatches in their plinths have been kept oiled.
The Blackwood was planted, in rows, as a hunting park. It stopped keeping to the rows a long time ago.
Hunters in the Blackwood hang lanterns to find the road home. The lanterns here are still lit, and nobody tends them.
The Cathedral of Ash was built over something older, with thicker walls than a cathedral needs.
The fire in the cathedral has no fuel that anyone can find. It has burned since before the pilgrims' grandmothers were born.
What the people of the river towns call the Sunken Crypt has no bodies in it. The niches are the wrong shape for bodies.
The river was not always in the crypt. Somebody opened a gate and let it in, and it was not an accident.
The keepers of the Roost fed something every day for three centuries, on the strength of a standing order.
The king of the Frozen Citadel ordered his own gates frozen. The order was obeyed at once, as all his orders were.
Cold of the citadel's kind does not come from the mountain. It comes from the walls, and it hums.
There are stairs under the last hall that are on no plan. The court called what went down them 'the remainder'.
The Hollow Throne was never empty. That is not the same as saying a king sat on it.
The Everbound feared neither age nor sickness. What they feared was being forgotten.
The oldest dragons were not born. They were commissioned.
A shield may withstand a thousand blades, yet fail the hand that raises it too late.
The ruins beneath the Cathedral predate the kingdom that built it.
